newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian state to hold on to about 60 firms.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian state to hold on to about 60 firms.

text.p: The Egyptian minister in charge of privatisation said in an interview published on Wednesday that the privatisation programme would draw to a close in the year 2000, by when the state would have a majority in only about 60 firms.
Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid, whose ministry runs about 300 state companies, also gave a new list of 14 companies slated for sale to principal investors in the first half of this year.

He said the state would hold on a majority in pharmaceutical companies, milling companies with total milling capacity of four million tonnes a year, monopoly companies such as cigarette manufacturers, the aluminium, sugar and public transport companies and some big iron, steel and textile plants.
The minister gave new figures for the proceeds from privatisation in 1996, when the programme began to gather pace.
He said the state had already received 3,650 million pounds from 1996 and was collecting a further 450 million pounds.

It paid 1,878 million to banks to pay off the debts of public-sector companies. Company employees received 152 million pounds and 1,620 million went to a Finance Ministry bank account, the minister said.
"I expect to sell tranches of shares in 20 companies for a value of 4.7 billion pounds in the first half of 1997," he said.

The minister said that in 35 to 50 percent of cases the state would sell to a main investor, in other cases to the public through the stock exchange. But he did not say what public flotations to expect in the first half of 1997.
